transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… things at work have gotten hard to keep straight. Tickets, receipts, notes, customer jobs—everything ends up piled together, and then I don’t know what to handle first.
Did you have these kinds of problems with staying organized when you were a child?
Yes… I think so. In grade school, teachers used to tell my mother I was bright, but kind of scattered. I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, lose papers, and need reminding to finish my work.
Do you get distracted easily when you’re trying to focus on a task?

Yes… pretty easily. I’ll start checking the day’s dry-cleaning orders, and after a few minutes my mind’s somewhere else—labels, choir things, stuff at home. Then I look back and realize I missed a bunch of what I was supposed to be checking.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to be moving or have trouble sitting still?
Yeah… I do. In meetings at church, or those fabric-care trainings, I keep finding little reasons to get up—water, papers, checking something. Everyone else is sitting, and I’m… not.
Do these problems with staying organized and focused also cause trouble for you at home?

At home… yes, some. It’s harder to keep track of things than I’d like. And it kind of spills over into the shop too—late orders, billing getting mixed up, people getting irritated with me.

At church I’ve backed off from some planning things, because… well, folks were getting frustrated, and I didn’t want to keep causing problems.
Have these focus and organization problems been present for most of your life, even during times when you were not especially stressed or worried?

Yes… I think so. I mean, even back in grade school, teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but… scattered. Talking when I shouldn’t, losing papers, needing reminders to finish my work. So it wasn’t just when I was stressed.
Besides work and home, do these attention and organization problems also happen in other parts of your life?

Yes… mostly at the shop and at church, I guess. The shop has had late orders and billing mix-ups, and that’s caused some tense moments with staff and customers.

At church, I’ve stepped back from leading some planning things because people were getting frustrated with me.
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about many different things?
I don’t know… not really a lot of different things. I mean, I worry some, like anybody, but I wouldn’t say it takes up most of my day.
